subject.title: Orphaned lock files not cleared on gateway restart when PID matches current process

question: Should #49603 remain the focused current-PID session-lock lifecycle tracker, or should maintainers fold the remaining work into a broader session-lock recovery issue after defining the safe reclaim policy?
rationale: The code can identify some self-owned orphan locks today, but reclaiming locks from a live current PID crosses a data-integrity boundary that automation should not decide from source inspection alone.

options.title: Define Liveness-Backed Reclaim
options.body: Add an owner-approved heartbeat, lease, or equivalent progress signal and prove startup, restart recovery, active-writer preservation, and stuck-lock recovery together.

options.title: Keep Conservative Reclaim
options.body: Treat current startup/acquisition reclaim as enough and document that live same-PID locks remain bounded by existing watchdog and operator recovery behavior.

options.title: Refresh Linked PR First
options.body: Use the linked fork PR as source material only after it is rebased, made mergeable, and shown not to regress active in-process writes.

recommendation.title: Define Liveness-Backed Reclaim
recommendation.body: Add an owner-approved heartbeat, lease, or equivalent progress signal and prove startup, restart recovery, active-writer preservation, and stuck-lock recovery together.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent session-lock ownership evidence and broad lock/test maintenance history make this the best available routing owner for the liveness policy choice.
